label: Pepper Row ordering and kitchen display

doc: One of the fourteen allergens UK food law requires a restaurant to declare.
No dish containing, or possibly containing, a guest's declared allergen is fired without staff acknowledgement, and every ticket carrying it is flagged at its station.
Taking payment for a served order.
Cooking a fired order station by station until every ticket is bumped.
The part of an order one kitchen station cooks, shown on that station's screen.
One Pepper Row restaurant: Canal Street, Harbour or Market Hall.
What one location offers tonight, grouped into sections.
One dish with its price, its station and the allergens it contains or may contain.
Deciding what a location offers and in which sections, and taking a dish off when the kitchen runs out.
What one table asked for, with the allergens the guests declared.
Opening an order for a table and firing it to the kitchen.
Money taken for an order through the card processor, tip included.
A section of the kitchen line: grill, fry, saute, cold, pastry or the pass.
Pins every open ticket with an allergen alert to the top of the station screen.
find_conflicts and enforce_allergen_rule: refuses to fire an unacknowledged conflict and returns what tickets must flag.
The TypeScript kitchen display: one screen per station.
Taking a dish off a location's menu for the rest of service when the kitchen runs out, and restoring it.
Groups a location's available items into sections in service order; 86's and restores items.
The order state machine: open, fire, serve, void.
The FastAPI ordering service: menu, orders, the allergen check, ticket routing and the payment handoff.
Creates a Tillpoint payment intent and settles the order from the signed webhook; never sees card data.
The station screen: one card per open ticket, late tickets highlighted, a bump button.
Splits a fired order into one ticket per station, with the allergen alert on the stations that cook a flagged dish.
Client-side state: the open tickets of one station, oldest first.
